findings.detail: Runner selection and planned versus direct dispatch produce four invocation branches. Both runner kinds repeat the plan decision and journal/target wiring, requiring synchronized edits whenever dispatch options change.
findings.fix: Select the runner and arguments first, then use one planned dispatch branch and one direct dispatch branch, preserving the exception handler.
findings.title: Uncited: Execution dispatch duplicates the optional-plan branch.

findings.detail: The nested conditional and subsequent fallback obscure precedence among explicit, active and default deadlines. Understanding a lock wait requires reconstructing all four combinations of explicit and active deadline availability across two expressions.
findings.fix: Use explicit branches that select the available deadline, take the minimum when both exist, and apply IO_LIMIT when neither exists.
findings.title: Uncited: Nested conditionals obscure lock-deadline precedence.

findings.detail: Every variant's execution plan is constructed twice with identical parameters, first for summation and then for validation. This repeats list and dictionary allocation and duplicates timeout-parameter wiring for both runner and gate variants.
findings.fix: Construct each plan once in the variant loop, validate it, and accumulate its timeout sum.
findings.title: Uncited: Document accounting constructs each execution plan twice.

findings.detail: The test reads checked_plant_test.py and constructs its AST without consuming either value. It immediately loads the gate-module AST used by the remaining assertions, leaving an unnecessary file read and AST allocation on every invocation.
findings.fix: Remove the unused plant-module read and ast.parse assignment while retaining the gate-module parsing.
findings.title: Uncited: The supervision-limit test constructs an unused AST.

strengths: Execution plans provide a useful boundary between declared limits, dispatch and observations.
Process launches share one explicit deadline-checking boundary.
summary: Reviewed all 162 membership paths and their committed changes for simplification, confirming generated mirrors match canonical sources at both endpoints. Four optional cleanup opportunities remain; no files were changed or tests run.
